title: Lockfile entries without a SHA-2 integrity value
what: a package entry that carries no SHA-2 integrity value in the lockfile
impact: The install verifies nothing about the bytes it downloads, so a substituted tarball from a compromised registry or network path is accepted as the reviewed package.
remediation: Regenerate the lockfile against a registry that publishes integrity values and commit the result.
limitation: It matches a package entry that carries no SHA-2 integrity value in the lockfile in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A lockfile written by an old npm that only emitted sha1 shows up under the sha1 rule, not this one.

title: Lockfile integrity recorded with SHA-1
what: a lockfile whose integrity value is a SHA-1 digest
impact: SHA-1 collisions are practical for a motivated attacker, so the digest cannot prove that the installed tarball is the one the lockfile recorded.
remediation: Re-resolve the dependency with a current npm so the lockfile records a SHA-2 integrity value.
limitation: It matches a lockfile whose integrity value is a SHA-1 digest in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A package that genuinely publishes only sha1 is still reported; the digest strength is the finding.

title: Lockfile integrity field present but empty
what: an integrity field that is present but empty
impact: An empty field reads as verified to every tool that only checks for the key, while nothing is actually verified at install time.
remediation: Remove the empty field and regenerate the lockfile so it carries a real digest.
limitation: It matches an integrity field that is present but empty in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A lockfile written by a tool that emits an empty string deliberately is still reported; the empty value is the finding.

title: Lockfile resolves a package over cleartext HTTP
what: a lockfile entry that resolves its tarball over cleartext http
impact: Cleartext transport lets a network attacker replace the tarball in flight, and the integrity value only helps if it is checked against the substituted bytes.
remediation: Resolve the dependency over HTTPS and commit the regenerated lockfile.
limitation: It matches a lockfile entry that resolves its tarball over cleartext http in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A local mirror on loopback is still reported; record it as an accepted exception if that is the policy.

title: Lockfile resolves packages from a third-party registry host
what: a lockfile entry served by a host other than the configured public registry
impact: Every package in the tree is fetched from a host the review process never covered, so its publication controls and provenance are unknown.
remediation: Serve the dependency from the approved registry, or document the mirror and pin it with integrity.
limitation: It matches a lockfile entry served by a host other than the configured public registry in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: An internal Artifactory mirror is a deliberate configuration; record it as an accepted exception with its integrity policy.

title: Lockfile resolves a dependency from a local path
what: a lockfile entry resolved from a path on the build machine
impact: The tree is not reproducible from the lockfile alone, and the bytes that compile are whatever that path holds at build time.
remediation: Publish the package and depend on a registry version with integrity.
limitation: It matches a lockfile entry resolved from a path on the build machine in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A workspace link is a deliberate monorepo pattern; it is still reported because the lockfile cannot reproduce it elsewhere.

title: Lockfile resolves a dependency from a git remote
what: a lockfile entry fetched from a git remote instead of a registry tarball
impact: The code is outside the registry's signing and provenance controls, so the registry integrity model does not apply to it.
remediation: Replace the git dependency with a published version that carries an integrity value.
limitation: It matches a lockfile entry fetched from a git remote instead of a registry tarball in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A private registry that proxies git archives is still reported; the entry names a git remote.

title: Lockfile resolves a source archive instead of a package
what: a lockfile entry that points at a forge source archive
impact: The archive is generated on demand from a branch or tag, so the installed bytes are not the published artifact and carry no registry integrity value.
remediation: Depend on the published package, or vendor the archive with its digest recorded in review.
limitation: It matches a lockfile entry that points at a forge source archive in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: An archive URL pinned to a commit sha is immutable but still outside the registry; it is reported as the same source kind.

title: Lockfile resolves a package from a bare IP address
what: a lockfile entry served from an IP literal rather than a named host
impact: An IP literal bypasses the TLS name check, so the connection cannot prove it reached the host the review approved.
remediation: Serve packages from a named HTTPS host with a valid certificate.
limitation: It matches a lockfile entry served from an IP literal rather than a named host in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A loopback dev registry is reported as well; treat it as an accepted exception for local builds.

title: Lockfile nests duplicate copies of a package
what: a lockfile that nests a second copy of a package inside another dependency
impact: Two copies of the same package mean the tree ships code the top-level review never saw, and a patched top-level version can be shadowed by the nested one.
remediation: Deduplicate the tree and lift the dependency to the top level where it can be reviewed once.
limitation: It matches a lockfile that nests a second copy of a package inside another dependency in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A deliberate dual-version tree for a compatibility window is still reported; the duplicate is the finding.

title: Lockfile entry without a resolved version
what: a package entry that carries no version string
impact: Without a version the entry cannot be compared to an advisory range, so a vulnerable install is invisible to every version-based check.
remediation: Regenerate the lockfile so each package entry records the version that was installed.
limitation: It matches a package entry that carries no version string in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A link or workspace entry without a version is still reported; it cannot be version-checked either.

title: Lockfile resolved a prerelease build
what: a resolved version that is a prerelease build
impact: Prerelease builds sit outside most advisory ranges and outside the stability promises the project tested against.
remediation: Pin the first stable release once it exists, and record the review that approved the prerelease.
limitation: It matches a resolved version that is a prerelease build in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A project that ships prereleases on purpose is still reported; the version shape is the finding.

title: Lockfile records git or path dependencies as version 0.0.0
what: a package entry whose version is the git/path placeholder `0.0.0`
impact: The placeholder hides the real identity of the code, so version-based review and advisory matching cannot see what actually runs.
remediation: Replace the git or path dependency with a published, versioned package.
limitation: It matches a package entry whose version is the git/path placeholder `0.0.0` in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A deliberately published `0.0.0` bootstrap package is still reported; the placeholder is the finding.

title: Lockfile records a dependency that runs an install script
what: a package entry flagged as running an install script
impact: Install scripts execute with the build user's privileges before any review step, so the dependency's code runs even if the project never imports it.
remediation: Prefer packages without install scripts, or run installs with scripts disabled for the untrusted subset.
limitation: It matches a package entry flagged as running an install script in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A package with a build script that only prints a notice is still reported; the install hook is the finding.

title: Lockfile records a bundled dependency
what: a package entry that ships inside another dependency's tarball
impact: The bundled copy bypasses registry integrity for that package, so the outer package's tarball decides which bytes are installed.
remediation: Unbundle the dependency and let the registry serve it with its own integrity value.
limitation: It matches a package entry that ships inside another dependency's tarball in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A vendored runtime that cannot be published is still reported; the bundle is the finding.

title: Lockfile records a dependency the registry marks deprecated
what: a package entry that carries a deprecation notice
impact: A deprecated package stops receiving fixes, so defects and advisories in it stay unfixed while the project keeps shipping it.
remediation: Replace the package or pin and document the maintenance plan that replaces upstream support.
limitation: It matches a package entry that carries a deprecation notice in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A deprecated package kept deliberately for compatibility is still reported; the notice is the finding.

title: Lockfile records an optional dependency that fetches at install time
what: a package entry marked optional, which npm may fetch from the network during install
impact: Optional packages still execute install scripts when they resolve, so a failed or substituted fetch can add code paths the review never listed.
remediation: Drop optional dependencies the project does not need, or run installs with optional fetches disabled.
limitation: It matches a package entry marked optional, which npm may fetch from the network during install in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: An optional package used for platform binaries is still reported; record the accepted exception and its integrity policy.

title: Lockfile entry without licence metadata
what: a package entry that records no licence
impact: Redistribution rights cannot be established for a dependency whose licence is unknown, which blocks release review and downstream use.
remediation: Regenerate the lockfile with a registry that publishes licence metadata, and record the licence in review.
limitation: It matches a package entry that records no licence in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A package whose licence file exists but is not in the registry metadata is still reported; the lockfile is the evidence.

title: Lockfile drops a dependency's own requirements
what: a package entry that records no dependency requirements where the package declares some
impact: The transitive surface disappears from the lockfile, so the tree that installs is larger than the tree the review read.
remediation: Regenerate the lockfile with a tool that records transitive requirements, and review the resulting graph.
limitation: It matches a package entry that records no dependency requirements where the package declares some in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A package with genuinely no dependencies is still reported; confirm it against the registry metadata.

title: Lockfile entry records no supported Node version
what: a package entry that declares no supported Node runtime
impact: Nothing tells the build whether the package was tested on the runtime that executes it, so a mismatch fails at run time rather than at review.
remediation: Regenerate the lockfile so the engine constraint is recorded, and align it with the runtime the project ships.
limitation: It matches a package entry that declares no supported Node runtime in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A pure-data package with no runtime requirement is still reported; the missing constraint is the finding.

title: Lockfile without a lockfile format version
what: a lockfile that declares no format version
impact: Without the version field the installer guesses the format, and different npm releases can resolve different trees from the same file.
remediation: Regenerate the lockfile with the npm release the project supports, so the format version is explicit.
limitation: It matches a lockfile that declares no format version in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A lockfile produced by a tool that omits the field is still reported; the missing declaration is the finding.

title: Lockfile written in the legacy v1 format
what: a lockfile in the legacy v1 format, which records a weaker per-package provenance shape
impact: The old format records less provenance per package, so the review sees a weaker graph than a modern lockfile would give it.
remediation: Regenerate the lockfile with a current npm release and commit the v2/v3 result.
limitation: It matches a lockfile in the legacy v1 format, which records a weaker per-package provenance shape in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A repository that must support an old npm is still reported; the format is the finding.

title: Lockfile pins the public registry to a non-standard port
what: a lockfile entry that reaches the public registry on an explicit non-standard port
impact: The port is outside the host's published service definition, so the connection may terminate on a proxy whose controls are unknown.
remediation: Resolve through the standard HTTPS port, or document the proxy and verify its integrity behaviour.
limitation: It matches a lockfile entry that reaches the public registry on an explicit non-standard port in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A corporate TLS-inspecting proxy is still reported; record it as an accepted exception.

title: Lockfile resolves a package over SSH
what: a lockfile entry that fetches over SSH from a git remote
impact: The install trusts whatever host key and account the build machine holds, so the bytes that run are decided outside the registry.
remediation: Fetch over HTTPS from a registry entry with integrity, or pin the commit and verify the checkout digest.
limitation: It matches a lockfile entry that fetches over SSH from a git remote in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A private registry that speaks SSH internally is still reported; the entry names an SSH remote.

title: Lockfile resolves a bare tarball URL
what: a lockfile entry pointing straight at a `.tgz` file rather than a registry path
impact: The tarball is not served through the registry API, so its metadata, signatures and advisory linkage do not exist for that entry.
remediation: Publish the artifact to the registry and resolve it as a normal package.
limitation: It matches a lockfile entry pointing straight at a `.tgz` file rather than a registry path in the parsed package-lock.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A registry mirror that serves the same layout is still reported when the host is not the configured registry.
